1102583582400522.transcript: the actual efficient size of a company shrinking very rapidly. And so the future will be almost all startups. Finally, somebody said it. I completely agree with Naval Ravi Khan. I feel the size of an average company is going to drop to 30 employees. And this is something that future generations that are looking for wealth creation, jobs, opportunities need to keep in mind. Historically, our entire business education system has trained people who become the 10,001th employee in our MNC. Trust me, those kind of jobs are gone. Almost 95% of jobs in MNCs are going to be taken away by AI. And what that means is, theoretically speaking, there are only two kinds of roles that are going to remain. Either you become the entrepreneur or you become the person who works very closely with an entrepreneur. Now, both these kinds of personas need to learn how to build things from zero to one, how to build real businesses with real revenue, how to talk to customers, how to launch product. And this is exactly what the business education space in India and the world does not teach. And that's where Mesa comes into the picture. 1136191559197445.headline: The next decade belongs to builders
1136191559197445.body:
Large companies are becoming leaner, AI is automating layers of work that used to require headcount, and a growing share of opportunity is concentrating inside small, high-leverage teams, i.e. startups.

Most business programs was built for the old version of this economy: one with stable hierarchies, predictable career ladders, and large organizations hiring in bulk. 

Mesa was built for the version that's emerging. A curriculum centered on real business-building, founder collaboration, and the skills that actually matter when companies are small and execution is everything; launching products, understanding customers, generating revenue, and making decisions without a playbook. 

Cohort 2028 applications are open. Explore the program.
1136191559197445.transcript: the actual efficient size of a company shrinking very rapidly. And so the future will be almost all startups. Finally, somebody said it. I completely agree with Naval Ravi Khan. I feel the size of an average company is going to drop to 30 employees. And this is something that future generations that are looking for wealth creation, jobs, opportunities need to keep in mind. Historically, our entire business education system has trained people who become the 10,001th employee in our MNC. Trust me, those kind of jobs are gone. Almost 95 percent of jobs in MNC are going to be taken away by AI. And what that means is, theoretically speaking, there are only two kinds of roles that are going to remain. Either you become the entrepreneur or you become the person who works very closely with an entrepreneur. Both these kinds of personas need to learn how to build things from zero to one, how to build real businesses with real revenue, how to talk to customers, how to launch product. And this is exactly what the business education space in India and the world does not teach. And that's where Mesa comes into the picture. We've built a curriculum which is focused specifically on new age skills that develop entrepreneurs, that develop people who can work with entrepreneurs. We have an entire system of startups where students get to work on projects with startups to understand how decision making in startups works. We've got an entire system where each one of our students build a real business from scratch with real product, reaching revenues of almost one crore. We've got an in-house incubator and we've got a career prep engine that makes sure that each one of our students lands fantastic jobs where they get to work with founders directly solving very pressing problems for India's startup ecosystem. Built a voice first AI companion, pitched it to 50 plus VCs, scaled it to 1000 plus monthly active users. Another one built an AI powered tool that got him his dream job. Another pivoted entirely into AI and is now leading an AI product at a fast growing startup. The gap right now isn't between people who understand AI and people who don't. 1290720899885510.headline: The B-school built for builders
1290720899885510.body:
Mesa is selecting 200 ambitious individuals for a transformative year of startup leadership.

You'll be trained by founders, business leaders, and VCs through: 
- a new-age curriculum, 
- live projects with real startups,
- hands-on experience building your own ventures from scratch.

Graduate ready to either launch your own company or step into leadership roles at high-growth startups. Apply to Mesa's PGP in Startup Leadership now.
1290720899885510.transcript: As a student, imagine getting a chance to be in a meeting room with 100 plus founders who have built successful startups during the 12 month program that you are undergoing. I did a 24 month 2 year MBA during that entire tenure at Kellogg. I probably saw two CEOs and that two from afar. I know for a fact that it changes how students live. We here at Mesa have also built a smart model around how to engage with founders. We just don't do fyside chats, those are boring. We speak to founders, understand the problems their startups are facing and we write cases about them. Students solve these cases, present their findings to the founders, there are debates, there are discussions and hence the interaction also becomes very very very interesting. Many of these founders recruit students from us. Somebody does well in the case, they get straight a job offer or an internship offer. Almost 40% of our students get jobs through this medium which is founders coming on campus and getting impressed. Which I find incredible.

1156225250083296.headline: Developer? Learn the business side
1156225250083296.body:
A software developer with 10 years at top tech companies feels stuck. 
AI is automating more of his code, and moving into product or business means proving new skills. 

The fix: learn how a business runs, make real revenue from scratch, meet people in leadership roles and learn to build products, not just code. 

Ascend, Mesa's Hybrid PGP in Business, AI & Entrepreneurship, covers all four in 12 months of weekends. 

For professionals with 5+ years of experience. Apply now.
1156225250083296.transcript: Let me tell you a story of a software developer that I know. He's been in coding for 10 years, has worked for top companies, fang, startups, solving their most technical problems. He was telling me the other day that he feels stuck. AI is automating the code completely. So tomorrow, if he has to move to say product or business, he will not be able to justify his salary. So what does a person like this do? The number one, this person needs to invest time in learning basics of business, business models, P&Ls, unit economics. Number two, learn to do real revenue from scratch. Pick a D2C product, brand it, package it, manage suppliers, manage inventory, sell it online, build a website, do real sales, offline if required. Number three, network. Meet more people from diverse areas. Meet people who are in leadership positions. They can open doors for you that otherwise could not be opened. And number four, learn to build with AI. I know you're technical, but solving a problem someone asked you to solve within a technical framework is very different from building a tech product from scratch. Software developers specifically are naturally analytical and great at problem solving. So if they do these four things, they are sorted for the post-AI era of work.

1660152285750346.hook_text: 90% of mid-career professionals are not able to grow beyond a certain level.
1660152285750346.headline: Grow beyond one function
1660152285750346.body:
Most mid-career professionals don't stall for lack of talent. They stall because they've only ever done one thing. 

The fix, in four steps: 
1. Learn the basics: business models, P&Ls, unit economics 
2. Build something: pick a product, package it, sell it 
3. Meet people who are where you want to be 
4. Learn to build with AI 

Ascend, Mesa's Hybrid PGP in Business, AI & Entrepreneurship, puts all four into 12 months of weekends. For professionals with 5+ years of experience. Apply now.
1660152285750346.transcript: 90% of mid-career professionals are not able to grow beyond a certain level. They are not able to pivot into roles that they like and are not considered leadership material. And you know why? It's because they've gone too deep into just doing one thing throughout their careers and they know nothing besides that. It's the biggest mistake that 27 to 32 year olds usually make. So my advice to them is, number one, they need to learn the basics of business, business models. You need to learn PNL, unit economics. Number two, learn how to start something from zero to one. Pick a problem, pick a product, package it, brand it, build a website, do actual sales. Number three, meet more people, network a lot. I know the word networking is thrown around a lot, but it's more about quality discussions with people who come from diverse backgrounds who are in positions. You want to be in. And these people can then open doors for you that you felt were impossible to open. Number four, learn to build things with AI. That is the only way you're going to stay relevant. That is the only way you can keep adding 10x value to a company and to yourself. The regular working professional, 100% going to become irrelevant if they don't do these things.

967305892765565.hook_text: So should I tell you the number one mistake that mid-career working professionals make?
967305892765565.headline: The #1 mistake mid-career pros make
967305892765565.body:
The biggest career mistake isn't a bad job. It's getting paid to do one narrow thing for years. 

Accounting, finance, data, marketing, coding, sales: AI is getting good at narrow tasks. The roles higher up need people who understand the whole business, from P&Ls to customers, partnerships and teams. 

Ascend, Mesa's Hybrid PGP in Business, AI & Entrepreneurship, helps you go wide in 12 months of weekends. For professionals with 5+ years of experience. Apply now.
967305892765565.transcript: So should I tell you the number one mistake that mid-career working professionals make? So I'm talking about 27 to 32 year olds in a good job. The biggest mistake is the company they are working for is paying them to do one very specific task. Could be accounting, finance, data analysis, marketing, coding, sales, very narrow, very specific. So people restrict themselves to learning about just one thing and they keep going deeper just into one thing. Now what happens when AI comes in is that today, Claude can do accounting better than the best accountants in the world. So all the expertise you have accumulated stands for nothing. And as you go higher up in a hierarchy of a company, it requires people who are horizontal with their expertise. People who know businesses, they understand PNLs, they can build product, they can do sales, they can talk to customers, they can do partnerships, they can build teams, they can manage people. But unfortunately, these people don't end up learning these things. So my advice is simple. Learn to build solutions and products with AI. Learn basics of business like business models, basic PNL. Learn sales and entrepreneurship. Learn to learn something. Sell it and these can be game changers for their careers.

1801699367686717.hook_text: As a student, imagine getting a chance to be in a meeting room with 100 plus founders.
1801699367686717.headline: The B-school built for builders
1801699367686717.body:
Mesa is selecting 200 ambitious individuals for a transformative year of startup leadership.

You'll be trained by founders, business leaders, and VCs through: 
- a new-age curriculum, 
- live projects with real startups,
- hands-on experience building your own ventures from scratch.

Graduate ready to either launch your own company or step into leadership roles at high-growth startups. Apply to Mesa's PGP in Startup Leadership now.
1801699367686717.transcript: As a student, imagine getting a chance to be in a meeting room with 100 plus founders who have built successful startups during the 12 month program that you are undergoing. I did a 24 month 2 year MBA during that entire tenure at Kellogg. I probably saw two CEOs and that two from afar. I know for a fact that it changes how students live. We here at Mesa have also built a smart model around how to engage with founders. We just don't do fyside chats, those are boring. We speak to founders, understand the problems their startups are facing and we write cases about them. Students solve these cases, present their findings to the founders, there are debates, there are discussions and hence the interaction also becomes very very very interesting. Many of these founders recruit students from us. Somebody does well in the case, they get straight a job offer or an internship offer. Almost 40% of our students get jobs through this medium which is founders coming on campus and getting impressed. Which I find incredible.

1814711466416613.headline: The only B-school teaching AI agents & no-code
1814711466416613.body:
At Mesa, you'll build products, pitch to investors, and land roles at India's fastest-growing startups. 

This is the business school for builders.

Apply now to learn how to create an impact in the startup world. Applications open for the 5th cohort.
1814711466416613.transcript: In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell it. I've funded 200 plus startups and invested over 800 crores over the last 4 years and almost every startup founder comes back to me with the same problem. Hiring. Honestly founders struggle to find people they can depend on. People can take a part of the business and just run it. Founders are looking for people who've actually built something. And it could be very small but it has to have made real revenue. They're looking for people who have sold things, can use AI and have solved real business problems. And they're looking for people who can do the basics. Speaking well, working with data and staying very organized. I think this combination is hard to find. But I've found this new business school in Bangalore started by my friends called Mesa. One is a Harvard Business School alum and the other went to Kellogg. I visited their campus a while back and since then I've been telling every founder I meet to hire from there. And it comes down to one simple thing. In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell. These students have to pick a category, build a product and website, make content, run ads and then sell online and offline. So when you hire from Mesa you're not hiring someone you have to manage. You're hiring someone who's already done it, who's already sold, run ads and found real paying customers. You can hand them a problem and trust them to solve it. They can lead a team or own a number. And I think that's why 150 plus startups are already hiring from there now.

1073588615687166.body:
At Mesa, you'll build products, pitch to investors, and land roles at India's fastest-growing startups. 

This is the business school for builders.

Apply now to learn how to create an impact in the startup world. Applications open for the 5th cohort.
1073588615687166.transcript: I've funded 200 plus startups and invested over 800 crores over the last 4 years and almost every startup founder comes back to me with the same problem. Hiring. Honestly, founders struggle to find people they can depend on. People can take a part of the business and just run it. Founders are looking for people who've actually built something. And it could be very small, but it has to have made real revenue. They're looking for people who have sold things, can use AI and have solved real business problems. And they're looking for people who can do the basics. Speaking well, working with data and staying very organized. I think this combination is hard to find. But I found this new business school in Bangalore started by my friends called Mesa. One is a Harvard Business School alum and the other went to Kellogg. I visited their campus a while back and since then I've been telling every founder I meet to hire from them. And it comes down to one simple thing. In the first 8 weeks of their curriculum, every student has to sell 5 lakhs worth of product. Like really actually sell. These students have to pick a category, build a product and website, make content, run ads and then sell online and offline. So when you hire from Mesa, you're not hiring someone you have to manage. You're hiring someone who's already done it, who's already sold, run ads and found real paying customers. You can hand them a problem and trust them to solve it. They can lead a team or own a number. And I think that's why 150 plus startups are already hiring from there now.

Because they watch tutorials, but they've never sat down to think about what should I do with those tutorials. And because even the few who start don't have anyone to guide them through the finish line. Mesa solves exactly this. AI isn't a separate module you'll learn. It's woven into every single course. 150 plus hours of applied AI curriculum. And every student builds at least one real AI product before they graduate. Not a demo, not a toy project, something that works. For example, one of our students, an investment banker with zero tech background. Built a vice-first AI companion, pitched it to 50 plus VCs, scaled it to 1000 plus monthly active users. Another one built an AI-powered tool that got him his dream job. 1358399446249615.headline: The next decade belongs to builders
1358399446249615.body:
Large companies are becoming leaner, AI is automating layers of work that used to require headcount, and a growing share of opportunity is concentrating inside small, high-leverage teams, i.e. startups.

Most business programs was built for the old version of this economy: one with stable hierarchies, predictable career ladders, and large organizations hiring in bulk. 

Mesa was built for the version that's emerging. A curriculum centered on real business-building, founder collaboration, and the skills that actually matter when companies are small and execution is everything; launching products, understanding customers, generating revenue, and making decisions without a playbook. 

Cohort 2028 applications are open. Explore the program.
1358399446249615.transcript: the actual efficient size of a company shrinking very rapidly. And so the future will be almost all startups. Finally, somebody said it. I completely agree with Nauravika and I feel the size of an average company is going to drop to 30 employees. And this is something that future generations that are looking for wealth, creation, jobs, opportunities need to keep in mind. Historically, our entire business education system has trained people who become a 10,000 and one employee in a MNC. Trust me, those kind of jobs are gone. Almost 95% of jobs in MNCs are going to be taken away by AI and what that means is theoretically speaking. There are only two kinds of roles that are going to remain either. You become the entrepreneur or you become the person who works very closely with an entrepreneur. Now, both these kinds of personas need to learn how to build things from zero to one, how to build real businesses with real revenue, how to talk to customers, how to launch product, and this is exactly what the business education space in India and the world does not teach. And that's where Mesa comes into the picture. We've built a curriculum which is focused specifically on new age skills that develop entrepreneurs, that develop people who can work with entrepreneurs. We have an entire system of startups where students get to work on projects with startups to understand how decision-making startups works. We've got an entire system where each one of our students build a real business from scratch with real product, reaching revenues of almost one crore. We've got an in-house incubator and we've got a career prep engine that makes sure that each one of our students lands fantastic jobs where they get to work with founders directly solving very pressing problems for India's startup ecosystem. 2318701735670638.body:
Large companies are becoming leaner, AI is automating layers of work that used to require headcount, and a growing share of opportunity is concentrating inside small, high-leverage teams, i.e. startups.

Most business programs was built for the old version of this economy: one with stable hierarchies, predictable career ladders, and large organizations hiring in bulk. 

Mesa was built for the version that's emerging. A curriculum centered on real business-building, founder collaboration, and the skills that actually matter when companies are small and execution is everything; launching products, understanding customers, generating revenue, and making decisions without a playbook. 

Cohort 2028 applications are open. Explore the program.
2318701735670638.transcript: the actual efficient size of a company shrinking very rapidly. And so the future will be almost all startups. Finally, somebody said it. I completely agree with Nauravika and I feel the size of an average company is going to drop to 30 employees. And this is something that future generations that are looking for wealth creation, jobs, opportunities need to keep in mind. Historically, our entire business education system has trained people who become a 10,000 and one employee in a MNC. Trust me, those kind of jobs are gone. Almost 95% of jobs in MNCs are going to be taken away by AI and what that means is theoretically speaking. There are only two kinds of roles that are going to remain either. You become the entrepreneur or you become the person who works very closely with an entrepreneur. Now both these kinds of personas need to learn how to build things from 0 to 1, how to build real businesses with real revenue, how to talk to customers, how to launch product and this is exactly what the business education space in India and the world does not teach. And that's where Mesa comes into the picture. We've built a curriculum which is focused specifically on new age skills that develop entrepreneurs, that develop people who can work with entrepreneurs. We have an entire system of startups where students get to work on projects with startups to understand how decision-making startups works. We've got an entire system where each one of our students build a real business from scratch with real product, reaching revenues of almost one crore. We've got an in-house incubator and we've got a career prep engine that makes sure that each one of our students lands fantastic jobs, where they get to work with founders directly solving very pressing problems for India's startup ecosystem. If you are somebody who's interested then Mesa is still accepting applications, apply as quickly as possible.

And this AI agent got me an interview with the founder of GoDacy. Today, I work as an AI at GoDacy, where I manage multiple product categories across quick commerce platforms. So, I'm preparing for UPSC to building AI automations and working directly with the startup founder. That's how much my career pivoted in just 12 months.
